title: Epic edge proposal
description: The edge file the epic-sequencer writes for ONE Epic in the dependency-assessment workflow: the candidate <workDir>/candidates/edges.json, which jsonartifact.py validates against this file and publishes as <workDir>/edges.json. `depscore.py validate` then checks it against the tracker and `depscore.py apply-edges` applies it as beads `tracks` edges; the workflow records each `decisions` row in the matrix (`atw-matrix link drives|restsOn`, side architecture). The session runs no `put`, no `link` and no apply. The edge test and the foundation checklist are the agent-teams-workforce:epic-sequencing skill's.

edges.description: EVERY edge to or from the assessed Epic that passes the edge test, each owned standing edge it keeps included, and no edge that does not touch it.

withdrawn.description: Every owned standing edge (the context's `standing` with `owned: true`) that `edges` does not keep. An edge with `owned: false` is in neither list.

decisions.description: One row for each foundation layer and other architecture decision judged for the assessed Epic, kept or dropped, that a matrix entry states. A decision no matrix entry states gets no row; the reasoning names it.

Edge.description: One architecture dependency: an architecture decision `to` rests on should be designed from `from`'s requirements first, and no `effective` document settles it. `from` is elaborated before `to`; both are Epics.

from.description: The beads id of the Epic whose requirements should drive the decision.

to.description: The beads id of the Epic that rests on the decision.

reason.description: The architecture decision and whose requirements should drive it, in one line.

archCheck.description: The document id and heading the matrix returned for the decision this edge orders, the `lifecycle` it returned, and why that leaves the decision open; or that the lookup returned nothing. An edge without it is refused.

answers.description: Required only on an edge the context's `withdrawn` list covers: why the recorded withdrawal reason is wrong, on the architecture. Without it that edge is refused.

Decision.description: One decision the assessed Epic drives or rests on, and the matrix entry that states it. The workflow records it as `atw-matrix link <relationship> --from epic:<id> --to <entry> --side architecture [--heading <heading>]`.

relationship.description: `drives` when the Epic's requirements shape what the entry states; `restsOn` when the Epic relies on what the entry states as settled architecture. The matrix registry (matrix-kinds.json) defines both relationships and the entry kinds each may end at, and `atw-matrix link` refuses any other.

entry.description: The id of the matrix entry that states the decision: a feature or a document for `drives`; a feature, document, stack, service, component or infrastructure for `restsOn`.

heading.description: For a document entry, the heading that holds the decision; "" for any other entry.
